speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the rash first appeared and whether it started on your face or trunk before spreading? Also, have you noticed any pain in your joints or swelling in your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash on her trunk and extremities appear to have a "slapped cheek" appearance on the face, and is the body rash lacy or reticular in pattern? Have you noticed any swelling or pain in her hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the mouth followed by a lacy, pruritic body rash is classic for Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. I will confirm this clinical diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
